title:
Everyday information.
Spoken aloud.
description: An Android assistive app for blind and visually impaired users.
narration: Meet AI Blind Assistant, an Android app that turns object observations and printed text into spoken information.
Let's follow a user's journey.
note: Current Flutter app • edited emulator walkthrough

title:
Start from
a clear Home.
description: Choose assistance, switch modes, or open preferences.
narration: From Home, the user opens Mobile Mode or chooses another feature.
Large labelled controls expose the assistance status, while TalkBack support and on-demand permissions make the interface easier to explore.
note: Native Flutter interface • no user account required

title:
Set a comfortable
way to receive alerts.
narration: Before starting, the user chooses audio, vibration, or both.
Detection sensitivity and announcement pacing can be adjusted to reduce distracting repetition.
Accessibility options include large text and high contrast. Preferences are saved locally.
note: Bounded haptics • local settings • adjustable feedback

title:
Start assistance.
Hear what matters.
description: The phone processes its camera input locally.
narration: The user opens Mobile Mode and starts assistance.
The bundled object detector runs on the phone. Its alert policy selects relevant object names and relative directions for offline speech and finite vibration.
The user can pause, resume, or stop. Visual risk is estimated; this is not exact distance measurement.
note: Synthetic emulator camera • no accuracy or distance claim

title:
Aim at the page.
Scan when ready.
description: On-device OCR converts printed text into readable content.
narration: To read print, the user opens Scan Document from Modes, aims at the page, and chooses Scan when ready.
Local text recognition extracts the words for the spoken reader.
The demonstration uses synthetic print. Camera images are never sent to an AI provider.
note: Synthetic sample page • on-device text recognition

title:
Read at
your own pace.
description: Touch and contextual voice actions control the same reader.
narration: After scanning, the reader can speak the document aloud.
The user can pause, repeat, move between reading lines, spell words, and change reading speed.
Scan Again returns to framing and waits for another explicit scan.
Ask AI first creates an editable text draft; sending it is a separate choice.
note: Real synthetic OCR • narration added; emulator speech engine unavailable

title:
Use your voice.
Keep control local.
description: Approved app commands use deterministic routing.
narration: For hands-free operation, the open app supports Hey Vision AI and local commands for navigation, settings, and reader controls.
Typed commands offer another route.
These approved actions execute on the phone. Say goodbye to end the active command session.
note: Local command interface shown • speech recognition not benchmarked

title:
Connect a
Raspberry Pi cap.
description: An optional private-network workflow extends camera placement.
narration: The optional wearable uses a Raspberry Pi camera on a private network or phone hotspot.
The user discovers the device, establishes trust, and connects to start.
The Pi detects locally and sends compact alerts for phone speech. Physical hardware acceptance remains pending.
note: Connection interface only • no connected Pi demonstrated

title:
Ask a question.
Choose what to send.
description: Conversation uses an explicitly paired laptop.
narration: Smart AI adds general questions through an explicitly paired laptop running local Ollama.
An owner-enabled Gemini option accepts text only, with local fallback.
Pairing is optional: object awareness, document reading, and local app controls remain independent of this conversation service.
note: Optional setup interface • no laptop reply shown in this recording

title:
More information.
More user control.
description: Open → personalize → detect or read → pause and stop.
narration: The journey is simple: open, personalize, detect or read, then pause or stop when finished.
AI Blind Assistant supplements a white cane, guide dog, and user judgment. It never guarantees a clear path.
note: Assistive aid • not a substitute for established mobility support
